title: Natural tensor comparison for the localized open-site equivalence
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and U an open. The canonical equivalence E = Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U identifies sheaves of modules on the localized site over U with sheaves of modules on U.toScheme [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], using the restricted structure sheaf as coefficients. For every pair F,G of localized module sheaves there is an isomorphism E(F tensor G) ≅ E(F) tensor E(G), natural in both module maps, for the sheaf tensor structures [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. No K-flatness, boundedness or derived-category assumption is required.

source.place: Lemma 17.16.4; functorial tensor compatibility, with the localized-site pure-tensor construction spelled out in the proof

proof.text: Obtain the sheafification transport natural isomorphism. PresheafOfModules.pushforward₀OfCommRingCat is monoidal by Mathlib, and both module sheafification functors are monoidal localizations. Register the comparison as a Localization.Lifting and apply Localization.Monoidal.functorMonoidalOfComp. Invert its tensorator μIso and use OplaxMonoidal.δ_natural, with reversed equality, to obtain exactly the required tensor naturality.

proof_origin.place: Tensor comparison via Mathlib presheaf precomposition and monoidal localization; remaining step is transport of module sheafification.

theorem exists_localizedOpen_tensor_equivalence (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens) :
    letI : MonoidalCategory
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U)) :=
      SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory (X.sheaf.over U)
    let E := Equivalence.functor
      (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
      (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
      (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U)
    ∃ e : ∀ (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U)),
      E.obj (F ⊗ G) ≅ E.obj F ⊗ E.obj G,
      ∀ (F F' G G' : SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
        (f : F ⟶ F') (g : G ⟶ G'),
        E.map (f ⊗ₘ g) ≫ (e F' G').hom =
          (e F G).hom ≫ (E.map f ⊗ₘ E.map g)
